chunks: "Mobility is how fast a charge carrier drifts per unit electric field. Formally v d equals micro E , with units of cm² per volt-second.
A high mobility means carriers move quickly for a given field, so you get high conductivity and fast devices.
Physically, a carrier in a crystal is accelerated by the field, but every so often it scatters off a vibrating lattice atom or an ionized dopant, and loses its direction.
The average time between collisions is tau , and the drift velocity averages out to micro E with micro equals q tau over m^ , where m^ is the effective mass.
So lighter effective mass and longer scattering time give higher mobility.
In silicon at room temperature, electron mobility is about 1350 cm²/V·s in lightly doped material and hole mobility about 480.
Mobility drops as temperature rises because the lattice vibrates more, and drops as doping rises because ionized impurities scatter carriers.
Conductivity is carrier density times mobility times charge, so mobility matters as much as doping.
At very high fields the drift velocity saturates around 10 to the 7 cm/s, and that's what really limits transistor speed."
